fact_text: PSX charges listed companies an annual listing fee that starts at about PKR 0.1 million for existing listings and rises with company size to about PKR 2.5 million at the upper end.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PSX earns a new-listing fee on each IPO equal to about 0.1% of the issuing company's paid-up capital, subject to a cap of about PKR 1.5 million.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PSX charges a small fee on government sukuk auctions that run through the exchange, a revenue line the presenter sees as currently minor but able to grow with future auction sizes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PSX sells trading and company data to customers and earns data-vending fees, and the presenter credits a single large international data customer with a significant step-up in that revenue line.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PSX collects a trading fee on both legs of every trade, about PKR 3.5 from the buyer and about PKR 3.5 from the seller for each PKR 100,000 traded.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The presenter argues PSX has pricing power on trading fees, because a charge of roughly PKR 3.5 to 4 per PKR 100,000 is too small for traders to change their behaviour over.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Average daily traded value on PSX was about PKR 6 billion in 2023, according to the presenter.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Average daily traded value on PSX was about PKR 15 billion in 2024, roughly two and a half times the 2023 level, according to the presenter.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Daily traded value on PSX was reported at around PKR 40 billion in July and August 2025, according to the presenter.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The presenter's scenario: if average daily traded value reaches about PKR 65 billion, the trading-fee revenue category alone would add roughly PKR 1 billion a year to PSX earnings.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Individual investors account for roughly 60-70% of daily trading volume on PSX, and their frequent turnover is what the presenter identifies as the main driver of trading-fee revenue.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PSX's main costs are administrative salaries and some equipment fees, and it operates three offices, in Islamabad, Lahore and its Karachi headquarters.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Presenter expects PSX costs to rise only about 10-15%, and at most 20%, even if trading-driven revenue doubles, so most incremental revenue should flow to operating profit.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because PSX costs are sticky, its operating profit moves closely with trading value, and the presenter also expects its stakes in CDC and NCCPL to add profit that tracks trading volumes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The presenter's FY26 scenario assumes average daily traded value of about PKR 50-60 billion.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The presenter's FY27 scenario assumes average daily traded value of about PKR 80-90 billion, which he argues the market would price in forward-looking.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The presenter's FY26 EPS estimate for PSX is roughly PKR 2 to 4 per share, depending on what average daily traded value turns out to be.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The presenter says PSX has historically traded at about 15-20 times earnings, which he attributes to its monopoly position, good economics and expansion potential.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Roughly 500 brokerage houses are registered in Pakistan but there is only one exchange, so growth in trading value flows to PSX without a competing venue taking the fee.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PSX raised its single-session price movement limit from 5% to 10%, a change the presenter credits with lifting daily traded value because stocks now move enough to attract active traders.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The presenter argues that raising the price movement limit further, to 15%, would likely lift PSX daily traded value again by allowing bigger intraday price swings.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Around 2000, when the 5% price limit applied, PSX daily traded value was a larger share of market capitalisation than it is today, according to the presenter.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Material inflation data, results announcements, government policy changes and even foreign-leader remarks cause price swings, and the presenter links those swings to surges in PSX trading and turnover.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PSX owns about 40% of the Central Depository Company, which holds investors' shares in custody and is the custody monopoly in the market.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: CDC charges about PKR 3.6 for each PKR 100,000 of shares moved from a broker account into an investor account.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: CDC's annual custody charge is about PKR 5.6 for each PKR 100,000 of shares held in custody.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: CDC also earns an annual account-maintenance fee of roughly PKR 400 to 1,000 on every brokerage account.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The presenter argues CDC has pricing power: a small annual custody fee rise, for example from about PKR 560 to 700 on a large holding, would barely change investor behaviour while lifting CDC profit sharply.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

company: National Clearing Company of Pakistan Limited
fact_text: PSX owns about 23% of the National Clearing Company of Pakistan Limited, which clears and settles trades.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

company: National Clearing Company of Pakistan Limited
fact_text: NCCPL charges about PKR 4 on the buyer and about PKR 4 on the seller for each PKR 100,000 traded, as its clearing and trading fee.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

company: National Clearing Company of Pakistan Limited
fact_text: NCCPL also collects capital gains tax on investor profits and charges an annual collection fee of roughly PKR 2,500 for large investment sizes and PKR 400-800 for smaller ones.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PSX also owns about 28% of PMEX, the commodities exchange, and about 12.5% of VIS, a credit rating agency; the presenter says neither makes much profit yet.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited - Everything You Need to Know' (YouTube transcript, undated)
